key_insight: Pretrained ViT features can be 'steered' toward user-specified or less-salient concepts via lightweight directional adjustments in feature space, enabling targeted visual representations without full model retraining.
problem_solved: Standard pretrained ViTs emphasize the most salient cues and lack mechanisms to direct their attention toward less prominent or user-defined concepts; multimodal LLM guidance tends to be language-centric and can dilute pure visual specificity.
method: Define steering signals from text prompts or exemplar images and learn compact steering vectors/adapters that operate in pretrained ViT feature space (minimal or no fine-tuning of the backbone).
Apply steering via linear modulation or attention reweighting to shift representations toward desired concepts while preserving overall feature utility.
Train steering modules with contrastive or alignment objectives so steered features better serve downstream tasks like retrieval, classification, and segmentation.
impact: Provides practitioners a low-cost, flexible way to adapt general-purpose visual representations to focus on specific, possibly subtle concepts—improving performance on targeted retrieval and fine-grained tasks without expensive model re-training.
visual_elements: Side-by-side attention/saliency maps: original ViT attention vs. steered attention highlighting previously suppressed concepts.
Pipeline diagram: pretrained ViT -> steering vector/adapter insertion point -> steered features -> downstream head.
Embedding visualization (t-SNE/UMAP): class clusters before and after steering showing concept separation.
Bar/line chart: downstream task performance (retrieval/classification/segmentation) comparing baseline vs. steered representations.
paper_authors: Jona Ruthardt, Manu Gaur, Deva Ramanan, Makarand Tapaswi, Yuki M. Asano
